subject: history
title: Détente to Collapse 1969-91
welcome_lead: SALT, Reagan and Gorbachev: the unwinding of the Cold War.
meta_desc: A-Level history adventure on détente, the Second Cold War, Gorbachev and 1989-91.
final_note: You have heard the hammer fall on the Soviet flag.

concepts.def: Easing of US-Soviet tensions c. 1969-79 marked by arms control, summits and economic exchange.
Strategic Arms Limitation Treaty signed by Nixon and Brezhnev on 26 May 1972 capping ICBMs and SLBMs.
1 August 1975 agreement recognising borders and committing signatories to human rights.

walkthroughs.body_html: Nixon-Kissinger triangular diplomacy opened relations with China in February 1972 and produced SALT I in May 1972. The 1975 Helsinki Accords legitimised post-war borders while embedding human-rights baskets exploited by dissidents. Détente collapsed after the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan on 24 December 1979; Carter withdrew SALT II and boycotted the 1980 Moscow Olympics.

Reagan's 1983 Strategic Defence Initiative and arms build-up pressured Soviet finances. Gorbachev's accession in March 1985 brought glasnost and perestroika. INF Treaty (December 1987) eliminated medium-range missiles. Withdrawal from Afghanistan completed in February 1989. Acceptance that Warsaw Pact states could leave Soviet orbit opened the door to revolutions of 1989.

Polish Round Table talks in February 1989 brought Solidarity to power in June. Hungary opened its border in May; East Germans fled west. The Berlin Wall opened on 9 November 1989; Romania's revolution executed Ceausescu on 25 December. Germany reunified on 3 October 1990. The August 1991 coup against Gorbachev failed; the USSR was formally dissolved on 26 December 1991.

mcqs.q: Why did the superpowers pursue détente in the 1970s?
options: Détente meant the USSR converted to capitalism.
Mutual recognition of nuclear parity, US exhaustion from Vietnam, Soviet economic stagnation, and the cost of the arms race — formalised in SALT and the Helsinki Accords.
The Tet Offensive ended the Vietnam War in 1968.
Détente ended the Cold War in the 1970s.

mcqs.q: Why did the Soviet Union collapse in 1991?
options: The USSR collapsed because Reagan outspent it in the arms race.
A combination of economic stagnation, nationalist movements in republics, the failed August 1991 coup, and Gorbachev's reforms accelerating loss of control to Yeltsin.
Détente meant the USSR converted to capitalism.
The USSR collapsed because NATO invaded Moscow.

mcqs.q: What was the Tet Offensive's main significance?
options: The Tet Offensive was a military victory for the Viet Cong that drove out the US.
The Tet Offensive ended the Vietnam War in 1968.
Militarily the Viet Cong suffered heavy losses, but politically it shattered the US public belief that the war was being won, fuelling anti-war pressure on Johnson.
The USSR collapsed because NATO invaded Moscow.
